what_this_is: every failure the merge changed, classified. A merged branch inherits BOTH lineages' baselines, so the honest question is not 'did the count go up' but 'is any failure caused by this merge'.

resolved_by_the_merge.cause: grand-rapids-holland-mi was registered with no participation row, and a registered market with no row fails the assembler gate CLOSED FOR EVERY MARKET. Nothing could assemble at all: 30 errors in test_global_deployment_architecture_045 and 8 in test_launch_participation_046 were one cause.

cross_run_ledger_totals.why: assertions pinned the ledger's SIZE (143 discovery, 739 paid, 100 negatives) and grew when the union preserved Grand Rapids' history -- the union this order required
cross_run_ledger_totals.fix: each asserts its own market's contribution instead

lapsed_participation_pin.why: a signed authorization binds launch_participation_sha256, and listing the eleventh market lapsed it; the founder was asked and accepted the lapse
lapsed_participation_pin.fix: a narrow conftest helper answers 'nothing disagrees EXCEPT the lapsed pin' -- it drops only complaints about the participation record, so a dropped market, a changed contract or a moved control file still fails

inherited_indianapolis_baseline.proof: every one of the 17 was RUN on grok/ptf-indianapolis-revalidation-002 at d3d9a8c -- the commit that deployed Indianapolis to production -- and every one fails there. That branch fails 18; one of those passes here. Executed, not argued from provenance.
